cls: Prokinetic / gastrointestinal motility agent (benzamide; 5-HT4 agonist, 5-HT2 and D2 antagonist)
pharm: Substituted benzamide that stimulates upper-GI motility via 5-HT4 receptor agonism and 5-HT2/dopamine-D2 receptor antagonism, enhancing gastric emptying and lower-esophageal sphincter tone
quick: 1 mg three times daily before meals (range per local labeling)
Use with caution; limited data, consider dose reduction
Symptom response; extrapyramidal symptoms on prolonged use
summary: Cinitapride is a substituted-benzamide gastrointestinal prokinetic used (in countries such as India, parts of Europe and Latin America) for functional dyspepsia and gastro-oesophageal reflux disease. It is a 5-HT4 receptor agonist with 5-HT2 and dopamine-D2 antagonist activity, which accelerates gastric emptying and increases lower-oesophageal sphincter tone. It is taken before meals. It is NOT FDA-approved; the information here is based on EMA/SmPC, BNF and manufacturer prescribing data. As a benzamide/dopamine antagonist it can cause extrapyramidal effects and, like related prokinetics, warrants caution in patients at risk of cardiac conduction abnormalities; it should be avoided where GI motility stimulation is hazardous.
indications: Functional (non-ulcer) dyspepsia - symptoms such as postprandial fullness, early satiety, bloating, nausea
Gastro-oesophageal reflux disease (GERD) and associated dysmotility
Symptomatic gastroparesis / delayed gastric emptying (per local labeling)

dosage.d: 1 mg three times daily before meals
3 mg once or twice daily before meals
Use the lowest effective dose; consider reduction

admin: Take 15-30 minutes before meals to optimize the prokinetic effect
Use the lowest effective dose for the shortest necessary duration, especially in the elderly (extrapyramidal risk)
Avoid combining with other dopamine antagonists or drugs that prolong the QT interval
Re-evaluate continued need periodically; not for long-term uninterrupted use
moa: Cinitapride is a benzamide that acts as a 5-HT4 receptor agonist (enhancing acetylcholine release in the myenteric plexus) and as a 5-HT2 and dopamine D2 receptor antagonist. The net effect is increased upper-gastrointestinal motility - accelerated gastric emptying and increased lower-oesophageal sphincter pressure - relieving dysmotility-type dyspepsia and reflux symptoms.

absolute: Conditions where increased GI motility is harmful (GI haemorrhage, mechanical obstruction or perforation)
relative: Parkinson's disease or other movement disorders (dopamine antagonism)
Risk factors for QT prolongation / cardiac conduction disease
Concomitant CYP3A4 inhibitors or other dopamine antagonists
monitor: Cardiac status where conduction risk exists

preg: Safety in pregnancy has not been established; avoid use unless the potential benefit clearly outweighs the risk. (Not an FDA-approved product; based on EMA/SmPC guidance.)
lact: It is not known whether cinitapride is excreted in human milk; avoid use during breastfeeding because safety has not been established.
renal: There is limited data in renal impairment; use with caution and consider a reduced dose.
hepatic: There is limited data in hepatic impairment; use with caution as the drug is hepatically metabolized.

major: Drugs that prolong the QT interval / class IA and III antiarrhythmics - additive arrhythmia risk; avoid combination
Anticholinergics / opioids - antagonize the prokinetic effect
moderate: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g. azole antifungals, macrolides) - may raise cinitapride exposure; use caution
Other dopamine antagonists (antipsychotics, metoclopramide) - additive extrapyramidal effects
minor: Drugs whose absorption depends on gastric emptying - altered absorption rate
interactions.food: Take before meals; food timing affects the prokinetic benefit

rare: QT prolongation / cardiac arrhythmia (class effect caution)
emergency: Acute dystonic reaction (abnormal muscle spasms, eye rolling, neck twisting)
High fever with rigidity and altered consciousness (neuroleptic malignant syndrome)

monitoring: Symptom response and continued need for therapy
Extrapyramidal symptoms, especially in the elderly and with prolonged use
Cardiac status in patients with conduction risk factors
counsel: Take 15-30 minutes before meals as directed
It may cause drowsiness or dizziness - take care when driving or operating machinery and avoid alcohol
Report any abnormal involuntary movements, muscle stiffness or spasms, especially of the face or neck
Do not use long-term without review; tell your doctor about all other medicines
Avoid in pregnancy and breastfeeding unless advised by your doctor
pk: Prokinetic effect within ~1 hour of an oral dose
Plasma peak roughly 1-2 hours after oral administration
Supports three-times-daily dosing (or once/twice daily for SR forms)
Store at controlled room temperature, protected from moisture; keep out of reach of children
pearls: NOT FDA-approved - used in India, parts of Europe and Latin America; information here is from EMA/SmPC, BNF and manufacturer data rather than openFDA
Benzamide prokinetic with 5-HT4 agonist plus 5-HT2/D2 antagonist action - take before meals
Dopamine antagonism can cause extrapyramidal effects and hyperprolactinaemia - use the lowest effective dose, especially in the elderly
As with the prokinetic class, use cardiac caution and avoid combining with QT-prolonging drugs; do not use where GI motility stimulation is dangerous (obstruction, perforation, bleeding)
missed: If a dose is missed, take it as soon as you remember if it is well before the next meal/dose; if it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed dose. Do not take two doses together.
overdose: Overdose may cause drowsiness, GI upset and extrapyramidal symptoms. Management is supportive; anticholinergic agents (e.g. an antimuscarinic or, where appropriate, a benztropine-type drug) can be used for acute dystonic/extrapyramidal reactions. Monitor cardiac rhythm. Contact a poison control center.
